name: Narrow admissible tuple
description: Construct the largest admissible tuple within [0, 5000] by selecting a removed residue class for each prime. This is the fixed-diameter maximization formulation actually benchmarked in paper Table 2.

requirements.hardware: See upstream requirements and task notes.

notes: Runs the pinned original solve constructor with a candidate priority function and an independent exact certificate check. Paper search/model budget is not reproduced.
Uses the published Table 1/2/3 problem dimension, except minimum-maximal uses the n=16 training setting discussed in section 4.2.
Minimum-maximal uses positive cardinality with direction=minimize; this is equivalent to the paper negative-cardinality reward.

limitations: Execution interface inspected in pinned source. Full paper experiments have not been reproduced here.

The source itself uses a fixed diameter bound n=5000 and maximizes surviving tuple size. The local constructor directly returns integers in[0,5000]; for k distinct values it checks a missing residue for every prime<=k (larger primes cannot be fully occupied). The source instead evolves a prime-residue sieve priority. The mathematical feasible set/size objective are shared but candidate interface and search differ. MCTS-AHD ternary admissible sets are a different task and have been restored separately.
